measured.heard: Main calls factorial of 3, and factorial calls itself with n minus 1 until n is 1. Each call to factorial gets its own n and its own r, drawn here as one frame on the call stack. Now factorial of 3 cannot finish line 7 until factorial of 2 returns a value. So its frame waits above the new one. The empty box after r equals 3 times stands for the value factorial of 2 has not returned yet. Then factorial of 2 calls factorial of 1, so 3 factorial frames now sit below main. The next scene answers this question. In factorial of 1, n greater than 1 is false, so r stays 1 and it returns 1. Each factorial return hands its value to the call that made it 1 frame up. Factorial of 2 gets 1 and returns 2 times 1 equals 2. Then factorial of 3 gets 2 and returns 3 times 2 equals 6 to main. Main stores the returned 6 in its own r, then prints main got 6. The calls start in the order 3, 2, 1, and they finish in the reverse order. 1, 2, 3. The stack column grows by one frame for each factorial call and shrinks by 1 for each return. Each factorial return value flows up to the frame above.
